text:
Ava: following up on the pricing Q&A thread : quick place to drop clarifying answers on credits, bursts, and rate-limit behavior. ask here or paste customer snippets.
Rohit: first one we got from a PM: 'my demo used up credits way faster than expected. how do we estimate cost for streaming use-cases?'
Maya: streaming costs are still token-metered. estimate = prompt_tokens + streamed_response_tokens + tool_output_tokens. if you stream many small responses, overhead per-request can add up (metadata + handshake).
Elena: can we share a short example calc?
Maya: sure. example: 200 prompt tokens, streaming 800 tokens => ~1000 billable tokens. if model rate=0.0008/unit -> cost = 1000 * 0.0008. (we'll add a calc helper to KB).
Kenji: ops note: we cap rapid reconnects from a single token at a low health-check quota. repeated reconnects look like a DOS pattern and will be transiently throttled.
Rohit: what's our default reaction to sustained bursts above route quota? 429s only or adaptive behavior?
Ava: default self-serve: immediate 429 + Retry-After. For Dedicated we offer short in-queue buffering (configurable up to 10s) or automatic fallback to a cheaper model on overflow.
Elena: customers asked about "grace bursts" for traffic spikes during launches. policy?
Maya: we have a small graceburst window for accounts in good standing: a short soft boost (measured in tokens/minute) once per billing period. auto-approval is limited; larger bursts require a quick support request.
Rohit: do gracebursts consume credits or are they free?
Maya: they consume credits. think of them as temporary higher quota, not free units.
Kenji: SDK behaviour: on 429 we include headers: `x-rw-retry-after-seconds` and `x-rw-quota-token`. clients should use token-bucket friendly retry with jitter. sample:```js
// naive pattern
await fetchWithRetry(req, {backoff: 'jittered', maxRetries: 6});
```
Ava: we
re shipping an official helper that implements this pattern in our JS/Python SDKs. ETA: early next sprint.
Elena: what about per-route quotas vs org-level limits? where should teams configure burst tolerance?
Rohit: per-route quotas are the main control. org-level protective caps exist to catch abuse. product will add per-route burst profiles (low/med/high) that can be configured in Console next quarter.
Kenji: minor detail: healthcheck endpoints are exempt from billing but still count against a small separate health-check quota to avoid infinite loops bypassing protections.
Maya: question on credits top-ups: if billing adds credits mid-cycle, do we prorate?
Rohit: promocode/one-off grants prorate into the remaining period. monthly recurring credits apply at the start of the billing cycle. enterprise committed credits follow contract terms.
Elena: how do we show this in Console to avoid surprise for customers?
Ava: plan: Console alerting for 75/90/100% of credits + a per-route view that correlates token consumption to credits spent. UI sprint next week.
Maya: policy Q: will we auto-charge overage for self-serve accounts?
Rohit: nope. self-serve -> soft-throttle + email + webhook alert. enterprise/reserved -> overage billing by default with notification thresholds.
Kenji: internal-only: dev orgs get a separate dev-credit pool and higher soft caps. not exposed externally.
deploy-bot: KB stub for "credits & burst policy" created: https://intranet.redwood/KB/credits-burst-policy-stub
Ava: action items: Maya to publish the token-cost examples & KB tomorrow, Kenji to add SDK retry helper note to eng backlog, product to prototype Console usage overlay.
Rohit: thanks all  drop any follow-ups here and i'll collate for the KB.
